description: Fix the prompt-miner engine's CLI-entrypoint guard, which silently no-ops when invoked through the .claude/skills dir-symlink that SKILL.md Step 1 and the daily cron both prescribe. Council verdict PARTIAL-GO: ship the symlink-safe basename guard plus a probe that closes the blind spot both existing prompt-miner probes share (they hardcode the real .oh/ path); cut the else/process.exit(70) branch (refuted by construction — kills any host process importing the module) and the SKILL.md ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} repoint (premise measured in a non-skill shell). Explicitly does NOT fix NO-CORPUS: measured 2026-08-03, largest stratum is 6 at 24h and 9 at 168h against a floor of 10, and the cron has logged 19 NO-CORPUS + 4 NO-SESSIONS with zero markers ever mined.

acceptance_criteria: The .claude/skills invocation path produces a parseable dataset with sessionsScanned > 0

The new probe fails when the pre-fix guard is restored, and when the anti-pattern is added to any other .oh/skills/**/*.mjs in forward order, reverse operand order, or reverse order split across two lines
The new probe still passes with three comment-only occurrences of the anti-pattern present
No green->red probe transition versus upstream/development
Zero new skills, zero new CI jobs, exactly one new executable (the probe)
prd.md states the measured corpus ceiling and that NO-CORPUS is unchanged
rollback_conditions: Any green->red probe regression beyond next-dev-prod, already REGRESSION on development
Any change to a file in the always-loaded set
Any SKILL.md or agent description: frontmatter change
final_handoff_requirements: Companion issues #692, #693 and #694 filed and the #663 close comment carrying the ceiling table, before #663 is closed

userStories.title: The documented invocation path runs
userStories.description: As an agent following SKILL.md Step 1 or the daily cron, I want mine-traces.mjs to actually execute when invoked through .claude/skills, so a silent exit 0 is never mistaken for an empty corpus.
acceptanceCriteria: node .claude/skills/prompt-miner/scripts/mine-traces.mjs --dry-run --no-git --fixtures-dir <fixtures> exits 0 with a parseable dataset and sessionsScanned > 0
The real .oh/skills/... path produces the same result
The guard is path.basename(process.argv[1] || '') === 'mine-traces.mjs' — the stricter rlm precedent, not weigh's .endsWith
The now-unused pathToFileURL import is removed (it had exactly one call site)
A header comment names the failure mode, issue #663, and both sibling precedents
node --test .oh/skills/prompt-miner/scripts/__tests__/mine-traces.test.mjs passes 19/19 and importing the module as a library still does not invoke main()
userStories.notes: No else branch. Critic 1 built the proposed else/process.exit(70) variant and ran it: importing the module from any non-*.test.mjs file exits the host process before the importer's next line, uncatchable around a static or dynamic import. The module deliberately exports DEFAULT_WEIGHTS, classifyLine and scoreSession. ROUND 2: critic 1 found (SEVERITY: M) that the basename form trusts basename(argv[1]) globally, not file identity — a DIFFERENT file named mine-traces.mjs that imports this module would fire main(), and without --dry-run would call writeReports(). Verified no such file exists (find . -name mine-traces.mjs). Deliberately NOT switched to a realpath comparison: that would be collision-safe but would leave three sibling engines with three different guards, re-creating the divergence this PR exists to end. Recorded in the engine header with the instruction to change all three together or none. Critic 1 also confirmed (SEVERITY: L) that .oh/evals/probes/*.sh is outside the CI shellcheck glob, downloaded shellcheck v0.10.0 and ran it on the new probe anyway: exit 0, zero findings at -S warning.

userStories.title: A probe catches the blind spot, not just the instance
userStories.description: As the harness, I want an eval probe that invokes the engine through a real directory symlink and rejects the anti-pattern repo-wide, so instance #4 is caught mechanically rather than by a cron agent rediscovering it.
acceptanceCriteria: Behavioral guard: the probe builds its own ln -s "$ROOT/.oh/skills" "$TMP/skills" rather than depending on .claude/skills being materialized, invokes the engine through it, and asserts exit 0, non-empty stdout, parseable JSON and sessionsScanned > 0
Static guard: no executable line under .oh/skills/**/*.mjs compares import.meta.url with === in EITHER operand order, nor hands process.argv to pathToFileURL(; comment lines excluded
Hermetic: --fixtures-dir plus --no-git; no network, no real traces
Honest exit 2 when node, the skill dir, the fixtures, or symlink support is absent
Mutation M1 — restoring the pre-fix guard turns the probe red on the behavioral assertion
Mutation M2a — forward-order anti-pattern in .oh/skills/rlm/scripts/query-context.mjs turns it red
Mutation M2b — REVERSE-order anti-pattern (pathToFileURL(...).href === import.meta.url) turns it red
Mutation M2c — reverse order split across two lines turns it red
Mutation M0 — the three comment-only occurrences present today do not trip the static guard
A row lands in .oh/evals/RESULTS.md via /eval
userStories.notes: prompt-miner-schema-compat.sh:14 and prompt-miner-weakness-record.sh:16 both hardcode SKILL_DIR="$ROOT/.oh/skills/prompt-miner", so both stayed green through 23 days of the defect being live. That shared blind spot is what US-002 closes. ROUND 2: critic 1 refuted the first version of the static guard (SEVERITY: H) — it matched only import.meta.url on the LEFT of ===, so the operand-reversed form passed the probe with the live defect in the tree; the critic appended exactly that line to rlm/scripts/query-context.mjs and got exit 0. Fixed by matching both operand orders plus a mechanism-level pathToFileURL([^)]*process.argv pattern that also catches the line-split form a pure operand-order regex cannot see.

userStories.title: The cron file stops contradicting itself
userStories.description: As an operator reading .oh/crons/prompt-miner.md, I want the kill-switch paragraph to describe the frontmatter that is actually tracked, so the file is not self-refuting.
acceptanceCriteria: The body describes the actual enabled: true state and the flip-to-false kill switch
The frontmatter is named as the single source of truth
schedule, timezone, enabled, preflight and every cap are unchanged — no behavior change
userStories.notes: Resolved toward the tracked state, deliberately against the council's initial lean toward disabling. The evidence for disabling (23 days, zero markers, an unreachable floor) is misleading: this cron filed #663. Its realized value has been defect discovery, not marker mining, so disabling it would remove the instrument that found the bug this PR fixes. ROUND 2: critic 2 attacked this as ratifying drift and produced the archaeology that settles it the other way — enabled: true was set by a dedicated commit, 'feat: enable the prompt-miner daily cron (#277)', landed 2026-06-25 in forward-sync 85d42384 (body line 622), ~5 weeks before this PR. The code was the deliberate, older, tracked state; the doc paragraph never caught up. Critic 2 also corroborated the authorship claim: #663 createdAt 2026-07-22T11:03:12Z is 2 seconds after .cron.log's 07-22 result line at 11:03:10.

userStories.title: The ceiling is on the record
userStories.description: As a future reader of #663, I want the measured corpus ceiling and the companion defects on the record, so this fix is never misread as 'prompt-miner is fixed'.
acceptanceCriteria: Companion issues filed against mifunedev/openharness, labeled prompt-miner, before #663 is closed: #692 (corpus floor — withinWindow firstTs at mine-traces.mjs:922-924, hardcoded project dir at :817, absent isSidechain), #693 (render-log-entry.sh:47 worktree log-loss), #694 (cron reaper logs WORKTREE_DIRTY forever for an orphaned worktree)

Scoped by fix session and verification rather than one-per-defect: #692 bundles the three engine collection defects because they share one fix and one question (does the ceiling move?); #693 is a helper-resolution fix; #694 is cron-runtime, not engine
The PR body and the #663 close comment carry the measured ceiling table
The close comment states plainly that NO-CORPUS is unchanged
userStories.notes: Critic 2 verified zero companion issues existed at council time — gh issue list --label prompt-miner returned only #663 — so 'file follow-ups' was an unexecuted promise until this story landed. Filed before the PR opened. #692 demands a decision (fix collection and re-measure / restratify the floor / re-scope the skill), not only a patch, because the observed max stratum across 23 cron days is 2,3,5,5,6,9 — fixing collection raises the ceiling but is not established to clear the floor of 10. ROUND 2: #694 added after critic 2 observed the PR was arguing 'keep the cron because its realized value is defect discovery' while leaving an open defect its own log had shouted for 15 consecutive days unfiled — the argument failing to pay its own bill.
